name: Pisana et al. energy-condition evidence: Hawking-Ellis classification eq. (19) of the Morse spacetime (13) with type-IV regions (Fig. 9); WEC violation on a region of CP^2 (Fig. 12); a type-IV point p=(1,0,0,0)

published_statement: Sec. IV.B (after eq. 19): 'Using the tetrad (18a)-(18c), the test reduces to checking the sign of r^8 + 4r^6 - 2(z^4 + 6z^2 - 4)r^4 - 4(5z^4 + 2z^2 - 2)r^2 + (z^4 - 2z^2 - 2)^2. This expression is positive, zero, or negative, corresponding to types I, II, and IV, respectively. These regions are shown in Fig. 9. Thus, the spacetime (13), having regions where the stress-energy tensor is type IV, violates all the standard energy conditions. We stress that this does not mean that the violations originate solely from the type IV region; energy-condition violations also occur in the type I and type II regions.' Fig. 9 caption: '...revealing that the energy-condition violations associated with type-IV regions occur on the critical level set.' Sec. IV.C: 'considering the vector field w^mu in (21), which is timelike by construction, we find regions where T_mu nu w^mu w^nu < 0. A two-dimensional projection of the region where this inequality holds (evaluated at x = t = 0) is shown in Fig. 12.' And: 'A more rigorous analysis ... would require a numerical point-wise classification ... Here, however, we merely argue for the existence of type-IV regions. For example, after numerically computing a tetrad for the metric (22), we consider the event p = (1, 0, 0, 0) in the U1 chart. With our specific numerical choice of tetrads, we found that the stress-energy tensor T_ab at p has complex eigenvalues ... So T_ab should be of Hawking-Ellis type IV. Because the classification varies continuously, an extended region must exist in which the tensor remains of type IV; in that region all the standard energy conditions are violated.' After (24): 'changing zeta merely shifts, thins, or expands the regions where the energy conditions are violated; it does not eliminate them altogether. Nonetheless, we expect that, with an appropriate choice of zeta and a suitable starting Riemannian metric, one might ... remove such regions completely -- at least for the Morse spacetime M.' No integrated or averaged energy-condition quantity appears anywhere in the paper. A grep for integrat/averaged/ANEC finds only the geodesic integration range and an 'averaged flare-out' condition (lines 3557, 3675), which is geometric and is not an energy condition.
published_hypotheses: Classical GR with T_mu nu := G_mu nu/8pi and 'no cosmological constant' for the standard energy conditions (Sec. II.A). SEC is written with 1/2 T g, so n = 4.

Morse spacetime: the Morse function f = (1/2)(-(x1)^2 + (x2)^2 + (x3)^2 + (x4)^2) of a 0-surgery (eq. 1); the Riemannian metric g_R = delta + df df induced on the graph of f in R^5 (eq. 11), which the paper calls an arbitrary choice; the Lorentzian metric from construction (2) with factor 2, i.e. zeta = 2 (eq. 12, written as (13)); only points outside an arbitrarily chosen 4-disk about the singular point z = r = 0 are considered.
Criterion (19) needs a tetrad in which the only nonzero T_ab are T00, T01, T11 and T22 = T33 (spherical symmetry), per Maeda-Harada [83].

CP^2 part: the Fubini-Study metric (23) with Lambda > 0, taken as Lambda = 6 for the numerics (Sec. IV.C, stated for the geodesic normalisation); the particular vector field w of (20)/(21), with its single index +3 zero in the U1 chart; construction (22) with factor 2 (zeta = 2); Cartesian coordinates (x, y, z, t) on U1.

The CP^2 energy-condition statements are numerical: Fig. 12 is a 2D projection at x = t = 0, and the type-IV verdict at p comes from 'our specific numerical choice of tetrads'. Whether T for the CP^2 metric includes a Lambda g term is not stated; the paper says Lambda 'plays the role of a cosmological constant', while Sec. II.A defines the conditions with none.
The existence of an extended type-IV region around p is argued by continuity of the classification.
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED (minor): formation.py:236 and :431 give the type-IV point as 'p = (1,0,0,0) on CP^2'. The paper says 'in the U1 chart' (Sec. IV.C). A coordinate 4-tuple names a point only with its chart. The point exists and is type IV (check F), so this is a precision gap, not an error.

DROPPED (hedge): formation.py:236 and :431 state 'a type-IV point' flatly. The paper hedges: 'we merely argue', 'with our specific numerical choice of tetrads', 'should be of Hawking-Ellis type IV'. The re-derivation removes the need for the hedge. The eigenvalues of the mixed tensor G^a_b at p do not depend on the frame, and they come out as -14 +- 10.583i (= -14 +- 4 sqrt 7 i) and -6 -+ 2 sqrt 2. So the tree's flat statement is now backed by a computation, but the owner did not have that computation when it wrote the line.

NOT NAMED by either the paper or the tree: formation.py:234-235 and :429 carry 'WEC violated, T_ab w^a w^b < 0, on a region of CP^2 (Fig. 12)' without the Lambda convention. The extent of the region depends on whether T = G/8pi or T = (G + Lambda g)/8pi. On the fine grid (|y|, |z| <= 0.6, step 0.025, x = t = 0) it is 154 points against 576. That a region exists holds under both conventions, and the type-IV verdict at p is convention-free because a Lambda term shifts every eigenvalue by the same real constant.

NOT NAMED in the evidence constant (weakened specificity): NUCLEATION_EC_EVIDENCE (formation.py:427-431) and the prose at :231-237 do not carry the paper's particular choices: zeta = 2, the Riemannian metric (11), the vector field (21) and Lambda = 6. The paper calls each choice arbitrary and expects that a suitable zeta and g_R might remove the violations from M altogether. The tree names zeta as free in NUCLEATION_FREE_FUNCTIONS (formation.py:423-424) and states the evidence as 'qualitative only' with no integrated figure. It never uses the evidence to claim that energy-condition violation is necessary for nucleation, and D24's nucleation part stays OPEN (formation.py:432, 1110-1112). The drift is one of labelling, not of use.

NOT NAMED (minor): the paper studies (13) only outside an arbitrarily chosen 4-disk about z = r = 0. The tree does not say so. This is harmless for the type-IV claim, because the type-IV set is unbounded along the critical level set (check E).

CANONICAL HYPOTHESES MATCH: 'the Hawking-Ellis type classification of T_ab as applied by the paper' and 'timelike w^mu on CP^2 as chosen by the paper' are faithful to the source. w is timelike at every grid point tested, and g_L(w,w) = -0.25 at p.

rederivation.outcome: ALL CHECKS AGREE (exit 0, 14 OK, 0 BAD); log at rederive/run.log. (A) (2) with (11) gives (12), which equals (13) exactly, with U = z^2 + r^2 + 1. (B) The characteristic discriminant of the (0,1) block of T^a_b is exactly (T00+T11)^2 - 4 T01^2 = (T00+2T01+T11)(T00-2T01+T11), which is criterion (19). One discrepancy, not a refutation: as printed, (19) makes the measure-zero case T01 = 0, T00 + T11 = 0 type II, while its source (Maeda-Harada Lemma 1) makes every T01 = 0 case type I. (C) z3 returns unsat for 'type IV and both null k = (1, +-1) have T(k,k) >= 0', and 133,454 random type-IV blocks all show a null vector with T(k,k) < 0. So type IV violates the NEC, and through the hierarchy every standard condition, as stated. (D) Tetrad (18) reproduces (13). In it the frame G_ab has only G00, G01, G11 and G22 = G33, so the precondition for (19) holds. (G00+G11)^2 - 4 G01^2 = [4/((z^2+r^2)^2 (z^2+r^2+1)^4)] times the paper's polynomial EXACTLY, and the prefactor is positive, so the paper's sign test is correct. (E) The type-IV set is nonempty: 5622 of 12880 grid points. On the critical level set r = |z| the polynomial is -32z^6 + 16z^2 + 4, which is type IV exactly for z^2 > (1+sqrt5)/4 = 0.809017. The degree-8 part (r^4 - z^4)^2 vanishes only on r = |z|, so far from the origin the type-IV set hugs the critical level set, consistent with the Fig. 9 caption. Near the singular point the level set is type I. 5082 of 7258 type-I grid points violate the NEC by Maeda-Harada Prop. 1, which confirms 'violations also occur in the type I ... regions'. (F) CP^2, U1 chart, Lambda = 6, computed with mpmath at dps 50 by central differences. The engine was checked on Fubini-Study (Ric = Lambda g, error 7.5e-25). At p = (1,0,0,0) the metric (22) has signature (-,+,+,+) with g_L(w,w) = -0.25. G^a_b has eigenvalues -14 +- 10.58300524i, -8.828427125 and -3.171572875: one complex pair, so the point is type IV, frame- and Lambda-convention-free and stable between h = 1e-12 and 1e-9. On the plane x = t = 0, T(w,w) < 0 on a 2D region near (|y| ~ 0-0.6, z ~ 0.05-0.4) under T = G/8pi, with a larger region under T = (G + Lambda g)/8pi, where the minimum of 8pi T(u,u) for unit u is about -1603. (G) The zeta scan is listed under data_at_publication. What is NOT re-derived: the shapes of Figs. 9 and 12 were not seen as images; only their content was recomputed.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. The result is a closed-form plus numerical computation of G_mu nu for two explicitly specified metrics, so no measured datum enters it and nothing the authors lacked in data can move it. Every exact claim the tree uses was re-derived: the polynomial agrees to within a positive factor, type IV implies NEC violation, the type-IV point at p is confirmed with frame-independent eigenvalues, and a WEC-violating region along w exists at x = t = 0. The real incompleteness is one the authors state themselves and is about model freedom, not data. The evidence is for one member of a family (zeta = 2, g_R of (11), w of (21), Lambda = 6), and the paper expects that a suitable zeta and g_R might remove M's violations completely. Here, for g_R of (11), the type-IV set survives every zeta sampled between 1.1 and 6. Whether any admissible choice removes the violations, and whether the CP^2 region can be removed at all, is not settled by the paper or by this audit. The tree already treats it that way: the evidence is 'qualitative only', there is no integrated figure, NUCLEATION_PRICED = False, and D24's nucleation part is OPEN. One more gap is an unstated convention, not a datum: the paper never says whether the CP^2 stress tensor carries the Lambda g term. It changes the size of the WEC region and neither its existence nor the type-IV verdict. Evidence either way: nothing found supports 'the authors lacked data'.
grade_evidence: The statement as the tree uses it (formation.py:66-69, 231-237, 427-432, 1110-1112) matches the source, arXiv:2505.02210v4, read in full at the relevant sections. The Morse metric, criterion (19) and the paper's printed polynomial were re-derived exactly in sympy: the discriminant is 4/((z^2+r^2)^2 (z^2+r^2+1)^4) times the paper's polynomial. Type IV implies NEC violation was machine-checked (z3 unsat). Type-IV regions exist and are unbounded along the critical level set, and the NEC also fails in type-I regions. The type-IV point p = (1,0,0,0) in U1 has G^a_b eigenvalues -14 +- 4 sqrt 7 i and -6 -+ 2 sqrt 2, a complex pair independent of frame and of the Lambda convention. A WEC-violating region along w exists at x = t = 0 under both conventions. 'No integrated energy-condition figure' is confirmed by reading. No measured datum enters. The recorded drifts are all minor and none enlarges what the tree claims: the U1 chart omitted, the paper's hedge dropped (now backed by computation), the Lambda convention unnamed (it moves only the extent of the WEC region), and the specific zeta, g_R and w not carried in the evidence constant (the tree treats the evidence as qualitative and keeps D24 OPEN). One misprint-class discrepancy in the source: the T01 = 0 edge case of (19) is measure zero and recorded, not quoted as an error.
what_would_change_the_grade: NARROWED if the tree ever used NUCLEATION_EC_EVIDENCE as evidence that energy-condition violation is necessary for this nucleation, or for the whole family (any zeta, g_R, w), since the paper claims it only for its chosen members and expects the violations might be removable from M. Also NARROWED if the WEC-region claim were quoted with an extent, because the extent depends on the unstated Lambda convention. WRONG only if a recomputation with the paper's own (13)/(18) or (21)-(23) gave a discriminant of a different sign, or real eigenvalues at p. Both were checked and agree here. OPEN would apply only to the unseen figure shapes, which are not what the tree uses.
